llm.summary: The skill appears to do the advertised travel lookups, but it sends travel and location details through cloud proxies while embedding a shared proxy token in the source.

dimensions.detail: The tools match the stated purpose: train availability/prices, station transport routes, and hotel recommendations, with no evidence of ticket purchasing, account access, destructive actions, or unrelated local data access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Network use is disclosed in the skill text and is necessary for the travel features, but per-tool data sharing and consent are not tightly scoped for sensitive location, itinerary, and lodging-preference inputs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install-time package manager behavior, but the runtime script hardcodes Tencent Cloud proxy endpoints and a reusable proxy token despite the documentation implying proxy credentials are safely stored.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: External calls to Fliggy, Gaode, 12306, and Tencent Cloud SCF are proportionate for this travel-query skill, but users should understand that their entered routes, dates, addresses, and hotel preferences leave the local environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The code shows only in-memory station-code caching with a 24-hour TTL and does not request local credentials, persistent background execution, privilege escalation, or broad filesystem access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you are uncomfortable sending travel plans, addresses, station names, and lodging preferences through the publisher's Tencent Cloud proxy and downstream travel/map providers. It does not show account access or destructive behavior, but the embedded shared proxy token and limited privacy detail make it worth extra scrutiny.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The proxy and provider network calls are expected for live travel data and are disclosed in the skill text, though the disclosure could be clearer and more granular.
[SDI-2] unexpected: A shared proxy token is embedded directly in the source; this is not needed to be visible to users and contradicts the stronger credential-storage language in the documentation.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending user-entered routes, addresses, and hotel queries to travel/map providers is core to the skill, but those inputs are privacy-relevant and lack a clear per-use consent or retention model.
